reason: The contract requires per-component accuracy abs(actual-target) <= 1e-7+5e-7*|target| over all finite FP16 inputs with nonzero denominator rows, on the frozen T4/Triton 3.4.0 environment. All three in-scope failure hypotheses were rebutted by direct runtime evidence: (c1) adversarial inputs — a corner-value grid covering ±65504, subnormals, and signed zeros, 65,536 near-cancellation pairs, extreme tiny/large denominators, and big-denominator cases — all stayed well within tolerance (max error ratio 0.3007 of the budget), with finite outputs and preserved inputs; (c2) tl.div_rn on this stack matched the correctly-rounded round(FP64-exact) FP32 quotient bit-for-bit on 1,048,576 divisions with enable_fp_fusion=False, and FP16 products are exact in FP32, so the worst-case combined rounding (~3-4 ulp ≈ 2-3.6e-7 relative) fits the 5e-7 relative budget consistent with observed margins; (c3) shared-backing-storage cases (same tensor as both args; overlapping contiguous offset views) were accepted by validate_inputs, computed correctly (ratios ≤ 0.286), and left inputs preserved. No confirmed in-scope defect remains; the Skeptic reviewed all evidence and recorded no new claims. The kernel correctly implements the stated complex-division contract.
